haiku-low.q1: By reads of reports.row_count: 10,000 or fewer streams the CSV in the click's response. More than 10,000 queues a background job; the user gets an emailed download link.
haiku-low.q2: The second click gets the existing queued or running export (HTTP 200) with its filters and cols. No new export starts, even with different filters.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours from send time. The exports bucket deletes every object after 7 days; unfinished multipart uploads are discarded after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts. After the last fails, the row is marked failed, the upload is aborted, and a failure email is sent. The page shows failed and re-enables the button.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. The report_exports bookkeeping lives on the primary database. reports.row_count may be read from the primary, which the document says to confirm.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports table on the primary database. The page polls GET /api/reports/{id}/export every 5 seconds while queued or running, so reopening shows the stored state.
haiku-low.q7: It never holds the whole file. It reads 5,000-row keyset pages and uploads 8 MB multipart parts as it goes, so memory stays around one buffer plus one page.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing is visible until the multipart upload completes, so partial data is never downloadable. The next attempt aborts the old upload and restarts from row 1.
haiku-low.q9: Copied from the page URL at click time into the filters and cols columns of report_exports. The job reads them from the row by export_id; the payload carries only the id.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running'). The database rejects a second active row, so the losing request gets the existing one.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be complete and its file_key saved. The signed link is made just before sending. If the export is already done, the job returns and does nothing.
haiku-low.q12: The server aborts the connection, so the browser reports a failed download instead of a truncated file. No record exists, and the user clicks again.

sonnet.q1: By reports.row_count (total unfiltered count): 10,000 or fewer takes the small path, more than 10,000 takes the large path. Small: the CSV is streamed back directly in the click's response (no job, nothing stored). Large: click returns at once (HTTP 202 {export_id, status:'queued'}); a background job writes the CSV to object storage and emails the user a download link valid 24 hours.
sonnet.q2: No new export is started. The insert hits the unique index, and the endpoint returns the existing queued/running row with HTTP 200, including its filters and cols (even if the new click had different filters). If that row is queued, has no job_id and is older than 2 minutes, it is re-enqueued.
sonnet.q3: The emailed link works 24 hours (signed_url ttl 86,400 s, generated just before sending). The exports bucket deletes every object after 7 days.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts total (waits of 60 s then 300 s between; each killed after 1,800 s). After the last fails, on_final_failure sets status 'failed' with an error, so the page shows failed and the button is enabled again; the upload is aborted best effort and the user gets a report_export_failed email (no report data). If the email fails it is only logged; nothing is downloadable.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only; report data is never read from the primary. (The report_exports bookkeeping table is on the primary; row_count may be read from the replica if required.)
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table on the primary database (status queued/running/done/failed). The page polls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/export every 5 seconds while queued or running (also on page load and after a click returns 200/202); it stops on done or failed. Because state is in the table, it survives reloads and shows when the user returns later; on done it shows 'Link sent by email'.
sonnet.q7: It streams via multipart upload. It keeps a single 8 MB byte buffer plus one page (5,000 rows, keyset paging from the replica), uploads a part whenever the buffer hits 8 MB, and uploads the remainder as the last part, then calls complete_multipart. About 113 parts for 900 MB; memory stays far under 512 MB.
sonnet.q8: Nothing is visible at the key, since the file is only published by complete_multipart. The next attempt aborts the old upload (abort_multipart using the saved upload_id, ignoring errors) and restarts from the top (row 1, after = 0); no resume cursor is stored. If all attempts die, the bucket discards the unfinished upload after 24 hours. (If the file was already completed and file_key is set, the retry skips the build.)
sonnet.q9: They are copied from the page URL at click time into the filters and cols columns of the report_exports row. The job payload carries only the export_id, and the job loads the row to read filters and cols.
sonnet.q10: The database: a partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running'). One insert succeeds; the other hits the index and gets the existing row back.
sonnet.q11: The file must have been built and published: complete_multipart succeeded and file_key is saved on the row (a fresh signed_url is made just before sending). If the job runs again and status is done (or failed), it returns and does nothing. If the file is finished (file_key set) but the export is not done, it skips the build and only redoes the link and email, then sets done.
sonnet.q12: If a query fails mid-stream, the connection is aborted rather than ended normally, so the browser reports a failed download instead of saving a truncated file. The user clicks again. Nothing is stored. (A stale row_count hiding a much larger report hits the 60 s request limit and fails the same way.)
